title: f120.2: SmtpRelayError — typed error enum for relay delivery
description:
Add a typed error enum for SMTP relay delivery operations in crates/smtp/src/relay_error.rs.

**What:** Define SmtpRelayError enum covering all failure modes of the outbound relay client.

**Algorithm:**
1. Create crates/smtp/src/relay_error.rs
2. Define:
   pub enum SmtpRelayError {
     Transient(String),   // 4xx response — retry with backoff
     Permanent(String),   // 5xx response — do not retry for this message
     TlsHandshake(String), // TLS negotiation failed
     Io(std::io::Error),  // network I/O error
     AuthFailed,          // SMTP AUTH rejected (535)
     ProtocolError(String), // malformed SMTP response from peer
   }
3. impl std::fmt::Display for SmtpRelayError — display code + reason string but never raw SMTP text
4. impl std::error::Error for SmtpRelayError
5. Add fn is_transient(&self) -> bool — returns true for Transient and Io (network errors)
6. Add fn is_permanent(&self) -> bool — returns true for Permanent, AuthFailed, ProtocolError
7. mod relay_error; pub use relay_error::SmtpRelayError; in lib.rs

**Defensive programming rules:**
- Error messages must never include raw SMTP response text (could contain partial credential echo)
- is_transient() and is_permanent() must be mutually exclusive and exhaustive (all variants covered)
- TlsHandshake is neither transient nor permanent for retry purposes — it marks the peer down

**Tests:**
- Test: SmtpRelayError::Transient('temporary failure') displays without crashing
- Test: is_transient() returns true for Transient, false for Permanent
- Test: is_permanent() returns true for Permanent and AuthFailed, false for Transient
- Test: SmtpRelayError Display output does not contain the word 'password' or 'credentials' (oracle: string comparison)
- All variants covered by match in test (exhaustive check)

**Acceptance:**
- cargo test -p usenet-ipfs-smtp passes
- cargo clippy -p usenet-ipfs-smtp -- -D warnings passes  
- cargo fmt --all produces no changes
- is_transient() and is_permanent() cover all variants with no overlap
